articles.headline: Norris: 'Incredible' Antonelli two levels above Russell all season
keyFacts: Reigning world champion Lando Norris said Kimi Antonelli has performed two levels above Mercedes team-mate George Russell all season.
Antonelli holds a 102-point championship lead and could become Formula 1's youngest-ever champion at the United States Grand Prix.
Antonelli stated he is not thinking about the title win yet and is taking the weekend one race at a time.
body: Kimi Antonelli: Lando Norris, Lewis Hamilton praise Mercedes driver ahead of first F1 2026 title win chance at United States GP

Reigning world champion Lando Norris says "incredible" champion-in-waiting Kimi Antonelli has performed "two levels above" George Russell all season; watch every United States GP session live on Sky Sports F1, starting with first practice at 6pm on Friday evening
Friday 23 October 2026 00:10, UK

Lando Norris believes Kimi Antonelli has done an "incredible job" to perform "two levels above" Mercedes team-mate George Russell this season, in form which has taken the Italian to the brink of a record-breaking world championship triumph.
Antonelli looks all but assured to succeed Norris as F1's reigning world champion this year thanks to the 102-point lead he holds at the top of the standings with six rounds left.

The 20-year-old could become the sport's youngest-ever champion as early as this Sunday's United States Grand Prix if he wins the race and nearest challengers Russell and Lewis Hamilton do not score sufficient points to stay in mathematical contention.
And Norris, who claimed his own maiden crown last year, has spoken glowingly about Antonelli's second season of F1 up against the "very good" Russell.
"I think it's very impressive what he's been able to do," said Norris.

"At his age, his second year in Formula 1, he's going to be the youngest world champion ever. It's pretty incredible, especially because, I wouldn't say he had a bad first season in Formula 1, he was against George, who I think is very good and has performed very well, especially in the last year [at Mercedes in 2024] against Lewis.
"For him to take quite a huge step from last year to this year, in terms of optimising things and understanding how to drive this year's car, more than other people as well.
"Dealing with the pressure, the lack of mistakes that have come from him, in both qualifying and races, the consistency to beat his team-mate.

"I rate George and I think he's a very good driver, but Kimi has been two levels above George the whole season. He's done a pretty incredible job and I'm sure the world knows that. I don't need to say it, I think it's obvious enough."

Mercedes made the then-18-year-old Antonelli the sport's third-youngest driver in history when they promoted him to the seat vacated by the Ferrari-bound Hamilton, F1's most successful-ever driver, from the 2025 season.
Asked in Austin on Thursday if he had any advice for Antonelli as his successor closes on the title, seven-time champion Hamilton quipped: "Slow down!
"No, I don't know. He doesn't need any advice. I think he's shown this year, and also last year, but particularly this year, his talent and his ability, his calmness and his approach.

"He's done an amazing job this year, and I'm so proud of him. I'm so proud of the way he's carried himself, how he interacts with the drivers and even with you guys. It's great to see him and the team excel. If it's not my team, I'd always want to see my old team do well
'Crazy if you think about it' - but Antonelli not thinking about title win yet

Although it has seemingly become a question in recent races of when and not if Antonelli will win this year's championship, the mathematics required for him to do so as early as Sunday evening in Austin are not in his own hands.

Antonelli would clinch the title if he claims his ninth race victory of the season and Russell finishes ninth or lower and Hamilton fifth or lower. That three-way result has not happened once so far this season.
"I mean, it definitely is crazy if you think about it, but that's why I won't think about it," said Antonelli.

"I've heard that something catastrophic needs to happen to the others for me to become champion. For me, it needs to be a perfect weekend. The others need to have a poor result, which is unlikely to happen.

"So, of course, anything can happen, and it's crazy to think about it. But, as I said, we had a meeting with Bono [Peter Bonnington, Antonelli's race engineer] this morning, and we just said, 'Just have fun.' It's always the same mindset I've had all year: one race at a time. Just try to do the best I can every race weekend, and then we'll see.
"But, of course, if I do things well, then the result will come."
The Italian is aware of the significance of what almost-certainly awaits him at some point in the forthcoming weeks, but is focused on making it a reality first.
"I mean, it would be a dream. It's something I've dreamt of since I was little," he added.
"First of all, to find myself in such a position is incredible. But at the same time, I need to keep going, keep pushing, and it's not over yet.
"So first, we'll try to finish the job properly, and then we can enjoy the rest. But, for sure, it would be an incredible achievement, but there's still a bit to go."

articles.headline: NFL Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk reveals he's been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease
keyFacts: NFL Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk revealed he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease a year and a half ago.
Faulk said early detection and medication have allowed him to effectively manage his symptoms and continue his daily life.
Parkinson's is a progressive brain disorder with no known cure that has affected several other former NFL players.
body: Hall of Fame running back Marshall Faulk has been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease, he revealed on an episode of the “Caring Neurologist” podcast published Wednesday .

Currently working as head coach at Southern University , Faulk said he has been dealing with the disorder for a year and half and caught it early, which has so far allowed for effective treatment. Parkinson’s disease is a progressive brain disorder most known for inducing tremors, with no known cure.
Faulk said he was diagnosed after noticing issues while playing golf and bring them up to his doctor:

“I get a physical twice a year. I’m a little anal about my health. I literally asked my doctor because I noticed it as I was playing golf. I noticed the rigidity in my hand after I play a lot or practice a lot, I thought it was just normal nerves when putting and stuff like that. But it started to be times where I wasn't playing — I mean, where I was playing, but I wasn't in a match, and it would still do that.
“I was like, ‘Wow, is that something? Is that normal?’ And the doctor was like, ‘You need to go get checked. You need to go have X, Y and Z done.’
Faulk emphasized the importance of early treatment and indicated that his medications have so far allowed him to continue living his life:

“Since I've started on the medication, I don't really have a lot of issues. I might sleep a little more … Other than that, the rigidity in my hands, I still have that. Can’t say that it’s gotten worse. The little tremors that I get, they are what they are. I just pay attention to my gait, how I walk, when I’m working out, my ability to balance. It’s still where it is.
“I don’t look at it as something that’s terminal. It’s like ‘Hey, you get to live with this.’ There’s far worse things out there.”

Neurodegenerative diseases like Parkinson’s are widely known as a risk that can come from long football careers, with a study earlier this year finding NFL players to have a Parkinson’s mortality risk nearly four times greater than the average person.
Brett Favre , Ahman Green and Bernie Kosar are among the former NFL players currently living with Parkinson’s. Another famous case was the late Muhammad Ali, who died in 2016.
Faulk recalled meeting Ali after his diagnosis and said he is now heartened by what he saw:

“I was at one his dinners at fight night and I sat next to him. He leaned over to me and he whispered, ‘You a bad boy.’ And then he made a couple other comments. I was like, ‘He’s all there.’ So knowing that, I didn’t look at it like life is going to end.

“I treat it like, I’ve had a bunch of surgeries on my right knee. There’s some parts of it that aren’t mine, that aren’t original. My back, it hurts every once in a while. It’s something you live with. It’s not a detriment to your livelihood. Now, if you don’t take of it, there’s an opportunity for that to be [a detriment]. But you do have to take care of it.”

Faulk has been enshrined in both the Pro Football Hall of Fame for his career with the St. Louis Rams and Indianapolis Colts as well as the College Football Hall of Fame for his time at San Diego State. He remains one of the greatest running backs in NFL history, and is the league’s only player to top 12,000 rushing yards and 6,000 receiving yards in his career.

A seven-time Pro Bowler as well as the 2000 NFL MVP and a Super Bowl XXXIV champion, Faulk began his coaching career last season as the running backs coach at Colorado. He’s in his first season at Southern , which is currently 1-3.

articles.headline: Amazon is spending over $1 billion on a new nuclear energy project to power its next data centers — but will it really live up to the test?
keyFacts: Amazon plans to buy power from 12 proposed X-energy nuclear reactors in Indiana to supply electricity for its data centers and the regional grid.
The proposed facility could deliver 960 megawatts, with construction and commissioning dates remaining uncertain according to the article.
Regulatory approvals remain a key obstacle, though an X-energy representative indicated the facility could become operational during the mid-2030s.
body: - Amazon plans to buy power from 12 proposed Indiana nuclear reactors
- The proposed facility could deliver 960 megawatts to Indiana’s electricity grid
- X-energy’s Xe-100 reactors would use helium cooling and TRISO fuel
Amazon is backing a proposed nuclear power development in Indiana designed to supply electricity for its expanding data center operations and the regional grid.
The project involves 12 small modular reactors from X-energy, with a combined planned output of 960 megawatts, although construction and commissioning dates remain uncertain.

Amazon hasn’t disclosed the specific amount it is putting into the Indiana project, but it says it is “investing billions in nuclear energy projects” overall. This confirmation, coupled with its lead role in X-energy, suggests the commitment could plausibly exceed $1 billion, though that is speculation.
Twelve reactors face an uncertain road to operation
The planned installation would occupy the former Breed coal generating station site in Sullivan County, Indiana, where developers intend to establish new nuclear generating capacity.
Each Xe-100 reactor is designed to generate 80 megawatts using helium gas for cooling and specially engineered uranium fuel particles known as TRISO.
X-energy says TRISO fuel resists extreme temperatures, while the Xe-100 design aims to limit reliance on active safety systems during certain accident scenarios.
However, the proposed Indiana installation remains a development project, and the United States has yet to operate a commercial small modular reactor supplying electricity.

Amazon's partnership with X-energy dates back to 2024, when the technology company led a $700 million financing round supporting reactor development and fuel production preparations.
That funding included work on reactor licensing and the initial stage of a TRISO-X fuel manufacturing facility in Oak Ridge, Tennessee.
The Indiana proposal forms part of a separate ambition to introduce more than 5 gigawatts of nuclear generating capacity across the United States by 2039.
Amazon would purchase electricity from the proposed installation, providing developers with an expected customer while the project advances through planning and regulatory requirements.
“New technologies like this often need initial customers to help de-risk projects and provide funding so they can be built and scaled to commercial availability,” said an Amazon spokesperson.
Regulatory approvals could determine the timeline
Regulatory approvals remain a key obstacle, and coordinating construction across the proposed facility could complicate delivery.
Nuclear developers in America generally pursue either approval for a standard reactor design or authorization covering a specific installation and its location.
X-energy has reported progress toward a construction permit for a separate Texas development, but that authorization would not automatically approve its Indiana proposal.
The Texas project involves four reactors intended to support a Dow chemical manufacturing facility, substantially fewer units than the planned Indiana installation.
According to the South Bend Tribune, an X-energy representative indicated that the Indiana facility could become operational during the middle of the 2030s.
The representative warned that the schedule could change as the project progresses, so the mid-2030s estimate remains provisional.

articles.headline: Warhound raises $200M to engineer war dogs and arm them with Anduril gear
keyFacts: Warhound emerged from stealth with $200 million in funding at a $1.2 billion valuation to genetically engineer and supply working dogs for military and law enforcement use.
The company will use gene editing to improve the health and performance of breeds like the Belgian Malinois and German Shepherd, while Anduril will provide tactical gear and software.
Warhound stated that the first batch of cloned dogs is expected to be born early next year and enter service within two years.
body: Colossal Biosciences’ Ben Lamm and Andruil’s Palmer Luckey had an idea to genetically engineer war dogs for the U.S. military, law enforcement, and other emergency response teams. That idea, on Thursday, announced its emergence from stealth as Warhound, armed with $200 million in funding from investors including In-Q-Tel, Sequoia, and 8VC. The round values the company at $1.2 billion.

These are dogs that perform tasks that are dangerous for humans or difficult for machines, like bomb detection, searches, and other specialized operations. In its launch announcement, the company said that more than 80% of the working dogs used by the U.S. military come from Europe and less than half of them are fit for service.

So not only is there a dwindling supply of working dogs for these tasks, but the U.S. has also become increasingly reliant on foreign nations for dogs that play an important role in the U.S. military and in law enforcement. That is key for what Warhound is trying to do. The hope is that Colossial can use its technology to engineer dogs with “characteristics suited to demanding missions,” the company said in a press release.

Lamm told TechCrunch he met Luckey about a year ago at a conference, where the Anduril co-founder brought up doing more for working dogs in the U.S. military. The two kept in touch, and Lamm did more research, learning about the breeding issues. Many dogs do not make it through training because of genetic dispositions for issues like poor eyesight or the high possibilities of cancer, hip dysplasia, or muscle atrophy.

Lamm believed dogs could be enhanced for health, longevity and “for things like speed and agility or enhance olfactory sensors for bomb sniffing and whatnot,” he said. His team looked at the top-performing working dog breeds — the Belgian Malinois and German Shepherd — taking the cell lines from them and putting them in a biobank. From there, they will edit the genes, adding the ones that will make the dogs perform better while taking out the ones that won’t, to create “a new type of dog.”

Andruil, meanwhile, will provide software and hardware enhancement for items such as dog protection vests and eye goggles to assist the dogs and their handlers with matters like situational awareness and coordination.
He said to imagine, for example, bulletproof vests that have data sensors that give information back to the handlers so they can better understand what is happening.

“The idea is, if we make the dog safer, make it healthier, make it perform better, it’s going to perform better in the line of duty,” Lamm said. He added that Anduril’s additions aim to make the dogs safer and healthier outside of their genetic components, “on top of the dog, not in the dog.” He believes such enhancements will also protect the dogs’ human handlers better.
Luckey doesn’t own equity in the company and is only a partner, Lamm told TechCrunch, clarifying that Colossal owns equity in the business, which it supports with licensing its technology.

Colossal is currently known for its de-extinction efforts of animals like the dodo and the mammoth. As Lamm previously told TechCrunch, the company has been using AI, buying and building technology to help with gene cloning and the identification and reproduction of animal genes.

The first batch of dogs is about to be cloned and incubated and is expected to be born early next year, ideally entering service within the next two years, Lammn said. Another company owned by Colossal, Viagen, is partnering with Warhound to help clone the dogs. Lamm said Viagen’s tech has a high success rate with cloning and Colossal currently uses it for its program to help protect endangered species.

The startup doesn’t know yet how much it will charge for the dogs but expects to sell to parties like first responders, the Department of Defense, military service groups, and police forces. When asked about government approval, Lamm said the company has briefed many government groups about the business.

In terms of the responsibility and safety of civilians when it comes to releasing genetically enhanced dogs, Lamm said the dog will be trained like any military working dog and will be managed by whoever buys it.

The company said it is working under the guidance of the American Humane Society to help certify Warhound’s training program for the newly created dogs that will enter service. The hope is also that when these new military dogs retire, they will enter the Society’s Military Working Dog Reunification Program, which provides a home for retired military dogs— or another program the society offers to help dogs.

articles.headline: Trump defends Ohio Democrat’s estranged mother after Ramaswamy’s widely criticized campaign ad – live
keyFacts: Donald Trump defended Vivek Ramaswamy's campaign ad featuring the estranged mother of Democratic Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton.
Both Republicans and Democrats denounced the ad because Acton's mother lost custody after her husband was charged with sexually assaulting Acton.
Trump claimed the press ganged up on the mother and said her statements disqualify Acton from running for Ohio governor.
body: Trump defends Ohio Democrat’s estranged mother after Ramaswamy’s widely criticized campaign ad – live
Trump defends Amy Acton’s estranged mother, who stayed with her husband charged with raping her daughter, and touts Vivek Ramaswamy’s ‘well coordinated’ attack ad
Trump says 'the press has ganged up on' Amy Acton's estranged mother who stayed with husband charged with raping her daughter

At the White House on Thursday, Donald Trump blamed the media for, in his eyes, unfairly attacking the estranged mother of Amy Acton, the Democratic nominee for Ohio governor, after the candidate’s mother recorded a campaign ad for Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican nominee, in which she called the daughter she has not seen since she was 12 “a liar”.

The ad has been widely denounced this week by Republicans and Democrats because Acton’s mother lost custody of her children in 1978 after her husband, Acton’s stepfather, was charged with sexually assaulting his stepdaughter, who was 12 at the time.

Trump, who was informed on Wednesday by Karen Travers of ABC News that Acton had “suffered sexual abuse by her mother’s husband” as a child, offered his full support for the ad earlier on Thursday, without acknowledging that Acton’s mother was estranged because she had stayed with the man charged with assaulting her daughter.

The president was confronted with that fact by Kaitlan Collins of CNN as he left the White House on Thursday for a campaign rally in Iowa. “Why did you make no mention of the sexual abuse allegations that Amy Acton made against her stepfather who stayed married to her mother?” the CNN correspondent asked.

Trump again professed total ignorance of the sexual assault allegation and attacked the questioner instead. “What happened is the the press has ganged up on a woman making a horrible statement about her daughter. And I don’t know why she should be shielded, or the daughter should be-” Trump said.
“She accused her stepfather of child rape,” Collins explained.
“Wait a minute,” the president continued. “The mother made a horrible statement about the daughter. Said she was a dirty liar.”
Trump then complained to Collins that if his late mother had said made statements like that about him, “you’d be the first one to be broadcasting and you would have found nothing wrong with them”.
The president ignored Collins when she said “but the child abuse allegation is different”.
“The press has ganged up because you hate it, because that one ad should really win,” Trump went on.

“Look, if what the mother said about the daughter is half right, she has no right even running for the governor of Ohio,” the president, who has a long record of documented lies, said – suddenly claiming that making false statement should be disqualifying for a public official.
“What about what the daughter said about her mother?” Collins asked.
“I don’t know what the daughter said,” Trump replied, clinging to his ignorance like a life preserver. “I don’t know.”
“Her mother remained married her stepfather who sexually abused her when she was 12 years old,” Collins repeated.
“Well, when did she make that statement? Was it just recently?” Trump replied, apparently trying to cast doubt on the allegation that was, in fact, made in 1978.
After Collins and another reporter said Acton made the allegation a sa child in the 1970s, Trump said.
“You know, I have no idea. All I know is Amy Acton’s mother said horrible things about Amy Acton, calling her a liar and other things,” the president said. “And I say that she’s fair game.”
“You’re trying to help Amy Acton get elected – the press has teamed up to help Amy Acton get elected,” Trump repeated. “And that’s all it is.”

The US supreme court ruled on Thursday that New Hampshire students cannot use their school-issued ID cards as proof of identity to vote, handing a victory to the state’s Republicans.

House Bill 323, signed by New Hampshire’s Republican governor, Kelly Ayotte, requires government-issued IDs, such as a passport or driver license.
The Coalition for Open Democracy, a New Hampshire-based nonprofit, had sued to block the legislation, arguing that it raised unconstitutional barriers for the state’s young voting bloc.

articles.headline: Spotify says yes, it is busting people for using Family Plan sharing too widely
keyFacts: Spotify co-CEO Alex Norström confirmed that the company uses a new QR code verification method to catch Family plan users who do not live together.

body: Spotify co-CEO Alex Norström confirmed on this week’s earnings call that the company is trying to catch Spotify Family plan users who don’t actually live together with a new QR code verification method that requires scanning the plan manager’s phone. TechCrunch reports that in response to a question about the “crackdown,” he called it a “routine improvement” instead:
Spotify says yes, it is busting people for using Family Plan sharing too widely
Spotify’s co-CEO said it will keep tweaking verification as people ‘find holes around’ methods like its new QR codes over time.

This is not as much a crackdown as it is actually a routine improvement of our verification methods for our Family Plan. Family Plan has existed for a long while. It has been around for, I think it is now close to 12, 13 years in Spotify history, and it makes up a pretty significant proportion of our subscriber base.

As such, it is important for us to just make sure over time that we improve the verification methods that we have. There are certainly ways, over time, to find holes around it. As that happens, we figure out how to improve it over time. This is not something that has an end date. This is not an implementation that is going to complete. This is just ongoing routine.

This isn’t the first time Spotify has tried to limit sharing Family plans, which it says are only for people living in the same household. The new QR code verification method has forced some users to get creative to stay on their shared Premium subscriptions — the code refreshes every few seconds and anyone who misses the seven-day window to scan it gets banned from joining a different Family or Duo plan for 12 months.

articles.headline: 8 Cyberpunk 2077 Replay Ideas to Make Night City Feel Brand New
keyFacts: Polygon published a guide detailing eight self-guided replay strategies to make Cyberpunk 2077 feel fresh for returning players.
The article outlines various roleplaying ideas, such as playing as a dual-revolver Nomad, clearing Watson before the main heist, or doing a no-cyberware run.
Other suggested playstyles include using only quickhacks as a netrunner, relying solely on Gorilla Arms for brawling, or turning off the minimap to navigate via landmarks.
body: V is running out of time. That’s the premise of Cyberpunk 2077: a stolen chip is slowly rewriting their mind. The only way out of this particular predicament ushers V through a cast of fixers, rock stars, and corporate killers who all want something from you. And yet, despite those bewildering stakes, there’s a decent chance you spent most of your time in the game clearing gigs, scanning NCPD crime scenes, and wandering Night City’s neon alleys. Then the credits rolled and, within moments, you were back at the character creator.

You’re in good company: Cyberpunk 2077 draws you into that second (or third, or fourth) replay, no matter how many hours you already have in the game. While there’s new content to peruse, such as the brand-new Edgerunners 2 Update, which adds a perk that lets V dual-wield, there are plenty more self-guided replay strats that make this familiar game feel fresh. Here are eight rules to make Night City feel like a place you’ve never been.
8 Be a dual-revolver cowboy
Gig terms: Start as a Nomad, build around revolvers, and look the part.

Nomads are Night City’s outsiders — clans of drifters who live in the Badlands, beyond city limits. If you choose to be among them by selecting a Nomad origin for V, you’ll join the Aldecaldos, the clan that includes Panam Palmer, a hotheaded driver who can become your closest ally. That’s a fabulous setup for roleplaying as an old-fashioned cowboy who’s all about family. Lean into this by donning torn jeans and a hat, ride your bike everywhere, and build V around handguns (especially revolvers). Do so, and you can take advantage of a new trick: The Edgerunners 2 Update’s Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree lets V dual-wield pistols and revolvers from the Power category. If you’re on an older build, a single iron will still do. Just keep the roleplay consistent: Never leave the bike at home, treat every NPC like a neighbor, and let the revolvers do the talking.
7 Clear Watson before the heist
Gig terms: Don’t go to Konpeki Plaza until you’ve finished everything in Watson. Everything.

How long can you put off the biggest job of your life? In Cyberpunk 2077’s opening act, V and their partner Jackie take a job from the fixer Dex. It’s a heist at Konpeki Plaza that sets the rest of the game’s narrative in motion — but there’s nothing actually forcing you to start it. Some players won’t touch it until Watson is cleared, which involves tackling a stretch of gigs, cyberpsycho hunts, NCPD scanner hustles, and side jobs that can put you around level 20 before the heist.

One approach is to treat it as a shopping spree: Level up enough to get Mantis Blades or Gorilla Arms and double-jump legs, then talk to Jackie about Dex’s gig, so V walks into Konpeki Plaza with a signature loadout. Another is to play it as a character beat: This V is too savvy to take the biggest job of their life without a few favors in the bank, so they invest in gigs and scanner hustles as insurance, first. Or you could spend time chasing Street Cred, the reputation meter that unlocks better vendor gear and later gigs. Regardless, by the time you head into Konpeki Plaza, you’ll be overleveled, overequipped, and extremely prepared for the job that changes everything.
6 Do…less
Gig terms: Pick one lifepath, a couple of characters, and one fixer. Ignore everything else.

Completionism is fun, but taking a different tack on a replay can let you focus more deeply on a specific storyline or build. For example, you might decide to prioritize getting Johnny Silverhand, the rockstar whose digital ghost rides along in V’s head, out of their life. That means pursuing that priority at the expense of anything else (you know, like you probably would if you really had Keanu Reeves stuck in your head). That could mean never meeting Goro, the former Arasaka bodyguard, or Panam, Rogue, or Claire, and sticking to Judy among the supporting cast. Looking for other targeted run ideas? Try being a Valentinos loyalist who never leaves Heywood, a Voodoo Boys netrunner who never leaves Pacifica, or a Mox-only run that never leaves Judy’s side. Everyone you skip will still be waiting at the Afterlife on your next run.
5 Go all-natural (relatively speaking)
Gig terms: No cyberware beyond what the story installs for you. Zero exceptions. Even for armor.

Since Update 2.0, almost every piece of armor in Cyberpunk 2077 comes from cyberware, not clothes. Trying to play the game without it feels as strange as strolling into a gunfight wearing a cardigan — which makes this play style such a weirdly energizing prospect. A no-cyberware run means giving up the game’s better armor and a lot of your mobility. A katana, blocking, and a stealth or sniper build will likely be your best bets. Enjoy more freedom to play around with fashion, too: Since clothing is now mostly cosmetic, wear whatever you like. Just be forewarned: Your first run-in with a cyberpsycho will remind you exactly why everyone else installed the chrome.
4 Be a netrunner who never fires a gun
Gig terms: Hack, don’t shoot. Every kill comes from a quickhack.

Netrunners, or hackers who plug into enemy networks with a cyberdeck, use quickhacks to disable, distract, and kill enemies from a distance. At low levels, these short-range code attacks are quite weak, which can translate to a rough first few hours in the game. Survive that, though, and it becomes one of the most overpowered builds in the game: you can jump into a room and take out a group without firing a bullet. You can even remain unseen by chaining Memory Wipe followed by Cyberware Malfunction, which clears enemies without alerting anyone. You can invest absolutely nothing in stealth and the build still does it for you. Just remember: Your cyberdeck is your weapon now, so spend on anything that boosts your RAM.
3 Brawl with Gorilla Arms
Gig terms: Fists only, no hacking, and no other weapons.

Punch first! And then keep punching. The Gorilla Arms are the chrome for players who’d rather settle things up close. Here, a brawler run means no hacking and no weapons. Only the arms. Put your attribute points into Body, which powers the Blunt Weapon perks that directly buff Gorilla Arms, and add Reinforced Tendons, the double-jump legs, to close the distance. Now, with the Edgerunners 2 Update, you have even more options. Five Glamdocs around Night City can now restyle your Gorilla Arms, along with Mantis Blades, Monowire, and the Projectile Launch System. If you’re going to knock an enemy across a room with your bare hands, you might as well do it in hot pink.
2 Turn off the minimap
Gig terms: No minimap. Navigate solely by landmarks and (if you really need it) the map screen.

The absolute fastest way to rediscover Night City is to stop watching the corner of your screen. Turn the minimap off, and, while it may take longer for you to reach your ideal destination, you’ll almost certainly discover places you’ve never seen before. Night City is a vertical city of districts like Kabuki, Japantown, and Pacifica, each with its own landmarks and shortcuts, and you’ll learn them by heart. Use the skyline as your compass: Arasaka Tower looms over everything, just find it to get your bearings. If you want to go further, slow down. With this playstyle, aim for a 100-hour playthrough instead of a 30-hour one. Read every shard. Drive around slowly with the radio on. Play Cyberpunk 2077 like a neon neo-noir novel. It works surprisingly well.
1 Be a sellout
Gig terms: Play a Corpo, pick the self-interested option in every conversation, and side with whomever is winning.

Sometimes it is everyone for themselves, and that’s okay. Cyberpunk 2077 gives you three origins to choose from — Nomad, Street Kid, and Corpo. You can play each as you’d like, but some play styles seem to pair more nicely with some backstories than others. Think: A people’s hero Street Kid, a loyal Nomad who never leaves family behind, or a sleazy Corpo who sided with the cops whenever it seemed profitable to do so. Your origin unlocks its own dialogue options and consequences, so, for example, a Corpo sees doors a Street Kid never will. If being mean to pixels makes you feel bad in real life, this run is good practice. In Night City, everyone has a price. In this run, you’re finally naming yours.

articles.headline: Execution Staff Warned Of IV Problems During Christa Pike's Execution
keyFacts: Execution staff struggled to establish IV lines before Christa Pike survived two lethal injection doses during an execution attempt, her attorney wrote.
Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 killing of Colleen Slemmer, and state protocol lacks guidance if someone survives two injections.
Pike returned to prison after being hospitalized on a ventilator, and the incident brought renewed scrutiny to Tennessee execution procedures.
body: Tennessee execution team members failed multiple times to establish working IV lines in Christa Pike’s arms before her attempted execution and warned that some of her veins may have ruptured, or “blown,” before she was injected with pentobarbital, her attorney wrote in a court document filed Thursday.

The IV team went through about 10 needles and tried several IV sites on both arms, attorney Randy Spivey wrote in the document. They even struggled to push saline through the last IV site they established, Spivey wrote.

Pike, 50, was hospitalized after surviving two doses of pentobarbital as the state tried to execute her on Sept. 30 for the 1995 stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer. She was 18 when she tortured and killed Slemmer with her boyfriend, becoming one of the youngest women to be sentenced to death.
State protocol calls for a second dose of pentobarbital if the first doesn’t result in death, but it doesn’t spell out what to do if a person survives the second injection.

After being taken to a hospital, Pike was on a ventilator for several days. At one point, her attorneys did not expect her to survive. She ultimately regained consciousness and returned to prison after being discharged.
The failed execution has brought renewed scrutiny to how Tennessee carries out death sentences.

articles.headline: O'Neill bemoans marginal moments but are Celtic just not good enough?
keyFacts: Celtic suffered a 2-1 defeat to Celta Vigo, leaving them with three losses from three Europa League games and 35th in the standings.
Manager Martin O'Neill blamed refereeing decisions and missed chances, while former players James McFadden and Pat Bonner stated Celtic are not good enough at the European level.
Celtic will try to reverse their European form when they host Besiktas in their next match on 5 November.
body: - Published
Three Europa League games. Three defeats for Celtic. They are 35th of 36 teams in the competition after another European collapse, this time against Celta Vigo.
Only Ararat-Armenia and their inferior goal difference keeps the Scottish champions from propping up the table.

Off the back of Sunday's 7-1 drubbing of Hearts, there was hope Martin O'Neill's team had turned a corner. Instead, the disparity between their domestic dominance and European shortcomings was laid bare once more.
After Mika Baur swept Celtic in front on 47 minutes, they went into their shells and succumbed to a timid 2-1 defeat as Javi Rodriguez struck twice in three minutes.
O'Neill bemoaned refereeing decisions and marginal moments that went against his team, but are Celtic simply "not good enough" to compete in Europe?
That was the verdict of former Scotland attacker James McFadden after a Celtic collapse that is becoming all too familiar.
"The performances at this level haven't been good enough," he said on Sportsound. "Celtic are way short."

Celtic looked nailed on for the Champions League this season when they went into a 4-0 aggregate lead against Austrian champions LASK in the play-off round, before shipping five goals in 77 minutes to drop into the Europa League.
O'Neill's side have now lost their last four European matches, conceding 14 goals in the process. Only once before had they done so in the same season - in the 2017-18 Champions League.
"It seems as though Celtic struggle when there's a bit of adversity," McFadden added. "If something goes against them, the confidence drops, their heads drop, they stop playing forward.
"The ball goes back and across, inviting pressure, and there's no way they take the pressure off. That has been a theme."
'Deserved' loss or night of nearly moments?

After another disappointing night, O'Neill focused on moments that went against his team - a free-kick not given before Celta's equaliser and a Liam Scales header that flicked the top of the bar at 1-0.

"We conceded a free-kick and I thought a second before that we should have had a foul for us," O'Neill said. "They score from the free-kick and it knocks us a little bit. It gave them a bit of momentum.

"I think if [Liam] Scales' header goes in to make it 2-0, we get the three points. We've lost three matches now, remarkably we're still in with a chance [of progressing]. We've got to win here and got to win away from home.
"We take the lead in the game, if we get the second goal we win the match and it changes the whole dynamic. It didn't happen, that's it - we need to try to find a way to win European games."
Centre-back Liam Scales had by far the most touches of any Celtic player with 121, well ahead of left-back Kieran Tierney (79) and goalkeeper Sam Johnstone (69).
Goalscorer Baur admitted they did not do enough to win and was at a loss when asked what needs to change. "How we played second half, last 30 minutes, we deserved it in the end," Baur said.
When asked if he knew why his team collapsed in such a manner, he responded: "I cannot tell you, sorry.
"It can happen that you get a goal, they can score too, good team - you should then get control back, hold the ball a bit longer to take the momentum away from them. You should break that."
Celtic did not get control back, did not break Celta's momentum and ultimately paid the price.
"I don't think Celtic are good enough, individually and collectively, to take on a team that's eighth in La Liga," former Celtic goalkeeper Pat Bonner said on Sportsound.
"They moved the ball really well and Celtic couldn't get close to them.
"They are not good enough at this level. Celtic are paying big money for some players because the fans are demanding it and then they come in and aren't good enough."
Their next European outing comes on 5 November as they host Besiktas, trying to reverse their continental woes. Whether they can or not is another matter.

body: Hundreds of Ethiopians have crossed into Kenya, fleeing fighting in the border town of Moyale, which was reportedly prompted by loyalists publicly raising the flag of a neighbouring majority-Somali state.

Kenyan police said on Thursday that hundreds of Ethiopians, mostly women and children, crossed into Kenya through several entry points in Moyale, including the Sessi, Kore, Biashara, Foundation and Miti areas.
The people who crossed the border were fleeing tensions between leaders of Ethiopia’s Oromia and Somali regional states, according to Kenyan police.
The police reported gunfire and chaotic scenes in Moyale.
Ethiopian media reported that the fighting in Moyale started as a dispute over raising the flag of the Somali Regional State, a regional state in eastern Ethiopia, on Sunday.
Tensions escalated into fighting between forces from the Oromia and Somali regions.
Gunfire, chaos
The Kenya Red Cross said it was setting up temporary shelter and distributing essential items including cereal and porridge flour.
“The response will initially reach 1,000 households,” the Kenya Red Cross said in a statement on Thursday.
It added that experts were conducting an assessment to work out how many people were affected and what their needs were.
The regional clash is hundreds of kilometres away from a larger conflict in the northern Tigray region between government forces and a rebel alliance led by the Tigray People’s Liberation Front.

articles.headline: Hugging Face Announces AI Model to ‘Chat’ With DNA

body: A new AI model can connect DNA to human language, enabling scientists to interact with genetic code in new ways. Hugging Face announced the Carbon-X model on Thursday as the latest and most powerful in the company’s Carbon family, a group of AI models built to analyze DNA.

“Carbon-X allows researchers to ‘chat with DNA’ for the first time: They can provide a sequence and ask questions about it in natural language,” Hugging Face research scientist Lewis Tunstall told CNET via email.

The word “chat” doesn’t mean talking to your genome but rather using an AI as a conversational interface, allowing users to paste in a DNA sequence, ask a question in plain English and receive back an interpretation, prediction or explanation — like a chatbot for DNA analysis.
More from CNET

The most popular chatbots, such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude, are cloud-based models that don’t run on your computer. The processing happens remotely, and you get the results back. But if you’re working on confidential or proprietary research that you haven’t yet published, you might not want to share it with an AI company. “Researchers need models they can study, adapt and run with sensitive or unpublished sequences on their own hardware,” said Tunstall.

One of the nice things about smaller, specialized AI models like Carbon-X is that it can run without using someone else’s computer. Hugging Face says the model can also work in tandem with other AI agents.
DNAgents

To be clear, Carbon-X is not a lab machine, so it can’t physically sequence DNA. It can look at DNA, such as a DNA sequence in a text file, and you can ask questions about it. Tunstall said Carbon-X’s strongest area is the model’s ability to predict mutation effects and complete DNA sequences.
“Carbon-X is particularly strong at helping researchers investigate genetic variation, for example, predicting whether a change in a DNA sequence is likely to be harmful,” Tunstall said.
He also said that it can give another AI model access to a DNA specialist when it needs to extract information.

However, the model does have limitations, according to the company’s blog post. Carbon-X can mess up sequencing operations through miscounts, and it can also hallucinate, which means the model just makes up information. Hugging Face noted that the model may invent the identity or function of a sequence when a user does not provide sufficient information in the prompt.
The quality of Carbon-X’s output also tends to degrade when users ask the model to produce particularly long DNA sequences, according to the company.
Lightning fast

In September, Nvidia announced it would buy Hugging Face for a little under $13 billion. At the time, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang called the company a “vibrant home for the open model developer community.” Open models are AI models in which some aspects of how they were trained are publicly available.

The release of Carbon-X comes just weeks after OpenAI models began solving longstanding mathematics problems. The AI lab drew widespread backlash from academic researchers after its proprietary models solved several long-standing problems without consulting scientists or showing what work went into solving them.
But Carbon-X is an open model, so AI-savvy biologists can at least peek under the model’s proverbial hood and glimpse how it runs.

“We think researchers also need open alternatives whose capabilities, limitations and risks they can examine independently,” Tunstall said. “By releasing Carbon-X and its training recipe openly, we enable the wider scientific community to test where it works, identify where it fails and help improve it.”

articles.headline: New York City votes to end century-old horse-drawn carriage industry
keyFacts: The New York City Council voted 40-7 to ban horse-drawn carriages in the city by June 1, 2028.
Lawmakers introduced the legislation after a tourist died in June from a horse-drawn carriage accident.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani is expected to sign the bill, while the Transport Workers Union plans to sue.
body: The New York City Council has voted to end the Big Apple’s horse-drawn carriage industry, which has been around for more than 160 years.

The legislation passed in a 40-7 vote on Thursday afternoon. Its approval came just over a week after New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani made a deal with City Council Speaker Julie Menin to ban horse-drawn carriages in less than two years.

The end result of that agreement was Romanch’s Law, which was named after an 18-year-old tourist, Romanch Mahajan, who died in June after falling from a carriage when the horse ran away. His death, which was the first and only human fatality connected to a horse-carriage accident, sparked action from local lawmakers.

The bill effectively bans all horse-drawn carriages in New York City, including Central Park, by June 1, 2028. It also prohibits the approval of new carriage licenses and ensures a transition plan is in place.

Such a plan would presumably include protections for carriage workers and the removal of carriage horses. The legislation stipulates that no horses will be slaughtered or transferred to another horse-drawn carriage business. Instead, the measure mandates the “humane disposition of carriage horses.”
Mamdani still needs to sign the bill, which is guaranteed to happen given his support for city officials and animal rights advocates pushing the ban.
The mayor said his administration is committed to making sure carriage workers are “protected” and the horses are “safe.”

Advocates were largely concerned about the safety of the horses, with about 40 horses dying on the job since 1982. But the livelihoods of carriage operators, many of whom are immigrants, will be harmed by the bill’s enactment.

The Transport Workers Union is already planning to sue New York City once Mamdani signs the bill into law. More lawsuits may be filed, New York City Councilwoman Vickie Paladino predicted before the vote took place.

“There will be a lawsuit coming up because this is unconstitutional,” the Republican lawmaker told Fox News. “Intro 943 is unconstitutional. Lawsuits are going to be filed immediately after this effort is passed. They’re going to be tangled up in legalese.”
Regardless of legal threats, the City Council’s top leader is taking the bill’s passage as a win.

“Today’s historic vote marks our commitment to animal welfare, public safety, and protecting workers,” Menin posted on X after the final vote. “Thank you to my colleagues, the advocates, and the countless New Yorkers who have worked for years to make this day possible.”
TRUMP DECRIES MAMDANI DEAL TO BAN NEW YORK CITY HORSE CARRIAGES: ‘SO SAD’
Hours before the City Council voted, President Donald Trump complained about the city ending its century-old horse-drawn carriage industry for “political reasons.”
“It was a Great Tradition,” he wrote in part on Truth Social. “Another piece of History that’s gone. It will be missed!”

articles.headline: To Start The New Cyberpunk 2077 Edgerunners 2 Quest, Do These Two Things First
keyFacts: Developer CD Projekt RED released the 2.5 patch for Cyberpunk 2077, adding an Edgerunners 2 themed quest called Clampdown.
To start Clampdown, players must finish the main quest The Heist and complete at least two of Wakako's gigs.
Completing the Clampdown quest grants players an armor set and a weapon themed after the character King.
body: Cyberpunk 2077 may have come out six years ago, but developer CD Projekt RED has just released a new update. The 2.5 patch adds a plethora of fixes and features , and it's also themed after Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2, including a themed quest and rewards to boot.

The Edgerunners 2 mission is called Clampdown, and it serves as a prequel of sorts to the events of the anime's new season. It features character King and his crew, and thankfully, it has no spoilers for the actual show. Rather, it serves as an extension, further tying the Cyberpunk transmedia efforts with each other.

Depending on the progress you've made in the game, though, you may not automatically gain access to Clampdown. If you're wondering how to start the Edgerunners 2 mission Cyberpunk 2077 so you can dive straight into it and reap the new rewards, we've got you covered.
In This Article
How to Start Clampdown, The Edgerunners 2 Mission in Cyberpunk 2077
Where to Find Wakako Gig Locations in Cyberpunk 2077
Rewards for the Edgerunners 2 Mission in Cyberpunk 2077
How to Start Clampdown, The Edgerunners 2 Mission in Cyberpunk 2077
Upon downloading the 2.5 update and booting up the game, Clampdown isn't immediately available. Rather, there are two steps you need to tackle.

First, you must ensure that you've finished The Heist . This is part of the main questline, and essentially serves as the culmination of the first act of the story. As such, you'll naturally get to it. Make sure to fully finish it.

Then, you must complete at least two gigs with Wakako . Once you're done, you'll have to wait to receive a text message from her. I skipped time for 24 hours, and then for 12 hours, and the message was on my phone right after. You may need to actually open your phone to see it, however.
Keep an eye out from a text from Wakako, not a call.

This last step can be tricky. Gigs are everywhere on the map, but you never get an indication about who they correspond to until you get close to them. Depending on what you've decided to tackle in your playthrough thus far, you may have already fulfilled this requirement. In case you haven't, don't fret, as we've outlined how to complete the second step in the section below.
Where to Find Wakako Gig Locations in Cyberpunk 2077
Your mileage may vary, but we'll be detailing the Wakako gig locations in Cyberpunk 2077 as if you haven't done any of them yet. Remember that you only need two , and the order is indistinct.
There's a Wakako gig northeast of where she is located.

One of Wakako's first gigs is available in Westbrook, Japantown. From where Wakako is located, look for the gig icon on the upper right corner. The task is called We Have Your Wife, and it's a fairly simple rescue quest.
This gig will take you to an underground casino.

The second Wakako gig location is in Westbrook, Charter Hill. It's right next to the double-lane highway. Once you get closer to the map icon, you'll be granted access to Tyger and Vulture. It requires you to go underground and access a hidden casino, but it's fairly easy to just follow the map indicator to get there.
Clampdown is a full-on quest.

Once you're done with the second gig, all you have to do is wait to get the text message. As explained before, I skipped time for 24 hours, and then for 12 hours. Afterward, I opened V's phone, and the message was there, which is labeled as "a request from King." Read it and follow the prompts to gain access to Clampdown.
Rewards for the Edgerunners 2 Mission in Cyberpunk 2077

Clampdown is a fairly straightforward but quite fun quest. Along with learning a bit more about the backstory of King and his crew ahead of the show's events, you'll also gain access to an armor set and a weapon.
The armor set and gun are themed after King's own gear in Edgerunners 2.
Here's the list of rewards for the Edgerunners 2 mission in Cyberpunk 2077:
King's Coat (Outer Torso)
King's Bulletproof Vest (Inner Torso, +25 armor)
King's Glasses (Face)
King's Pants (Legs)
Icon America Dust Devil Utility Boots (Feet)
Coronation (Tier 4 Iconic Tech Revolver, +200 percent headshot damage multiplier, +75 percent armor penetration, 0.5 sec charge time, as well as two empty mod slots)
That's all there is to know about the Edgerunners 2 mission in Cyberpunk 2077. Be safe out there, choom.

articles.headline: My GOTY is $7 and has 253 Steam reviews
keyFacts: The PC Gamer author stated that the $7 indie game Stuntboost is their favorite game of 2026 so far.
Stuntboost is a fast-paced first-person movement game featuring toy-themed obstacle courses, skateboarding, and precision camera control.
The game includes over 40 levels, layered leaderboards, ghost replays, and hidden collectibles.
body: Fast-paced. 3D Platformer. Parkour. First-Person. Racing.

Those are the tags affixed to the Steam page for Stuntboost, a game that I've had trouble summing up with a clean label when asked about it. Stuntboost is a skateboarding game that sometimes features a car, a platformer with a speedometer, an ode to those shrunken bedroom maps popularized by early FPS modders.
It's also, quite easily, my favorite game of 2026 so far.

Yet, Stuntboost could've easily slipped under my radar. It's been out for a month and hasn't made a big splash on Steam—it's rated "Very Positive" with 253 reviews. I only found it through a friend's recommendation, and even then, the art style didn't immediately suggest it was my thing.

Stunboost's toy fingerboards and cardboard circuits give the impression of a chill, Hot Wheels-adjacent racer your child could enjoy, but unless that child is accomplished with a mouse and keyboard, that ain't happening. This is the only skateboarding game with a warning that suggests you play with a mouse, and it's immediately obvious why.
Once you learn a few techniques, Stuntboost looks like this:
And this.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
And this.

Despite its choice of vehicles, this thing's for FPS movement sickos—an exercise in precision camera control and first-person platforming. It's essentially a three button game (jump, crouch, grind) about gaining and maintaining speed. Many of its tracks are non-linear obstacle courses that ask you to find your own way across, and the devs actively encourage looking for shortcuts.

I've been obsessed (a word I'm not using lightly) with Stuntboost's 40+ levels for weeks now, replaying tracks and cutting seconds off my times to score the top medals. And once I have those medals, I get to work shaving hundredths of seconds to take the number one spot on my friend leaderboard. Oh man, this is a dangerous game for a friendly rivalry. I now live in fear of a Discord DM informing me that the PB I spent hours honing has been shattered.

But I honestly welcome the excuse to replay tracks, because Stuntboost's movement is fundamentally thrilling, and its maps are masterfully crafted with standard and absurd routing in mind. Its wide ramps, massive jumps, and daring speeds remind me a lot of Trackmania—my favorite racing series—but more specifically, a subset of "full speed" community tracks that never ask you to brake.

Stuntboost also nails a lot of little quality-of-life features that you rarely see in games with way larger budgets. Information about a track is revealed in stages: I can't see friends' times until I've beaten the track once, and global leaderboards are locked until I get the diamond medal. The ghost of my best time appears automatically, but I can also turn on the ghosts of my friends or anyone else on the leaderboard. I can even watch anyone's replay in full as long as I've discovered the same shortcuts they used—a smart touch (possibly inspired by Neon White) that prevents spoilers and entices me to search for what I've missed.
"It's like Neon White"
- Layered leaderboards
- Shortcuts
- First-person platforming

BUT: I never finished Neon White because the levels got overwhelming. Juggling cards and shooting mandatory targets sometimes made levels feel strict and suffocating. Stuntboost is simpler, faster, and improvisational.

Watching replays is a big deal, too, because it's primarily how I picked up on community techniques that opened my third eye: varial kickflips, grind hopping, speed storage. Every sloped surface is an opportunity for just a bit more speed and every ramp-shaped object—be it a plate, playing card, or three-ring binder—is a springboard that could send me across the map. The variability of a single track can be staggering.

Later worlds (which visit other rooms of the same house) expand beyond the skateboard with car levels that revolve around drifting, free roam scooter levels with S-K-A-T-E collectibles, and a longboard that can't jump. Some of these are just a neat palate cleanser, but the car levels are particularly spectacular for how they force me to relearn how I turn and, eventually, hit sick drifts that're impossible on the skateboard.
"It's like Trackmania"
- Ghosts
- High speed
- Wild tracks

BUT: Trackmania is a proper driving game, and Stuntboost is its own thing. Where Trackmania demands braking and cornering to improve track times, Stuntboost has no brake, lets you turn on a dime whenever, and encourages max speed at all costs. If I made a Trackmania, it'd be just like this.

Every level has a hidden tape that unlocks a free cam (excellent for scouting) and contributes to unlocking a set of bonus levels. I haven't played all of these yet, but I'm told there's a huge tower gauntlet with a fierce leaderboard race. There's also a speedrun mode that times a run of the complete game, board skins, and a daily challenge.

I am in awe of how unique and fun and fully-featured this thing is, and for $7. Frankly, it's an injustice that Stuntboost isn't one of the year's big indie success stories, but that's nothing new. The indie games that click for me always gravitate toward interesting movement mechanics or use of physics, and that rarely intersects with what PC gamers are currently going wild about (deckbuilders, autoshooters, and city builders mostly).

I've played lots of those—what I want are more games that make me feel alive and dangerous. Stuntboost has me vibrating in place, leaning into high-speed turns, and cursing a god I don't believe in. It's an intoxicating rush on a level I have not experienced before, and you should absolutely play it.

Morgan has been writing for PC Gamer since 2018, first as a freelancer and currently as a staff writer. He has also appeared on Polygon, Kotaku, Fanbyte, and PCGamesN. Before freelancing, he spent most of high school and all of college writing at small gaming sites that didn't pay him. He's very happy to have a real job now. articles.headline: Amazon Has a Sale on Magic: The Gathering Booster Boxes Even Before Black Friday Kicks Off
keyFacts: Amazon reduced prices on several Magic: The Gathering Play Booster Boxes ahead of Black Friday, according to IGN.
Discounted sets include crossover properties like Star Trek, Marvel, The Hobbit, and Avatar: The Last Airbender.
IGN reported that standard Play Booster Boxes are discounted while offering fans a cheaper alternative to Collector Boosters.
body: Has Magic: The Gathering ever been as popular as it is right now? It feels like the long-running card game is having a bit of a moment in terms of bringing fresh players in via its ever-growing roster of Universes Beyond crossover properties.

Rightly or wrongly, that means there are more people looking to build collections, whether they’re playing or collecting the cards, and it just so happens that Amazon has rolled out some price cuts on Play Booster Boxes - including the Star Trek one at 26% off just weeks before it even launches .

It’s worth reminding you that these are Play Booster Boxes, as opposed to Collector Booster ones. Aside from a massive difference in price, Collector Boosters are where you’ll find the most valuable cards in each set. With that caveat out of the way, here are the best Play Booster Box deals we’ve found so far.
Save On Magic: The Gathering Play Booster Boxes

Sure, that Star Trek deal is great, but it’s not the only Universes Beyond property seeing a price cut. In fact, you can find discounts on both Marvel sets, The Hobbit, and Avatar: The Last Airbender.
If you’re desperate for the new Darkhold Destiny set announced for next year, then good news: You can save on both the Marvel Spider-Man and Super Heroes Play Booster Boxes.

The former, while not a great set, does have some cool cards, and while it would have cost you $209.70 around this time last year, it’s down to $134.95 for 30 packs. Meanwhile, the much better Super Heroes set from June of this year has dropped from the same MSRP to $149.99.

Sticking with 2026 sets, The Hobbit Play Booster Box has dropped down to $161.93, which marks a 23% discount. Whether you’re looking for Smaug, Gollum, Bilbo, or any of the dwarves from the set, this is a great way to build out a collection - and you get a box topper included, too.
Rounding out our Universes Beyond sale offerings is Avatar: The Last Airbender. This set was a very pleasant surprise, and you can grab a box of 30 packs for $139.99 right now .

For Universes Within, you’ve got a few options to build out your collection and deck-building options. Play Booster Boxes for Lorwyn Eclipsed, Secrets of Strixhaven, and even the current set, Reality Fracture, are currently discounted.

Lorwyn Eclipsed Play Boosters are down to $118 per box, but we’d recommend hanging fire for a little while. The same product was around $11 cheaper recently, and we can see this being ripe for a Black Friday saving.
Secrets of Strixhaven is still my favorite set of 2026, and if you missed all the fun, then you can catch up with a 21% discount on a Play Booster Box . 30 packs for $129.99? Don’t mind if I do.

Reality Fracture is a little different, because it’s being sold by a third-party seller . Still, it’s the current set and is sitting at $153.98, so you’re saving around $10 from the MSRP. Not huge, sure, but it’s an awesome set.
For more on Magic: The Gathering, be sure to check out all we know about next year’s sets so far , including some in-universe returns and another Marvel set.

articles.headline: Tiger Woods drops major return hint as TGL decision made
keyFacts: Kevin Kisner said Tiger Woods wants to play a full schedule on his Jupiter Links team for the upcoming TGL season.
Kisner stated on a podcast that he was dropped from the team roster because Woods wanted to play.
Season three of TGL begins on December 27, and Woods may also target the Hero World Challenge in December.
body: Whisper it quietly, but Tiger Woods may be closing in on his return to golf.
Woods has been absent from the sport following a rollover crash in March which resulted in a five-year driving ban.
Woods’ last competitive tournament came at the 2024 Open Championship Getty
But a curious roster move on Woods’ TGL team has set tongues wagging about a potential comeback date.
Former US Ryder Cup vice captain Kevin Kisner had been on Woods’ Jupiter Links team for two seasons but was a notable omission when the five-man rosters for season three were released.
When he explained the surprise move, Kisner appeared to let slip Woods’ return to action was not so far away.
Did Kevin Kisner give away Tiger Woods’ comeback plans?
“Well, obviously, I’m not on the team anymore,” Kisner said on Barstool’s Fore Play podcast.
“I had a two-year contract with Jupiter Links and then they, Tiger wants to play. And then they wanted to sign Keith Mitchell, which is totally fine with me.

“And I’m sure I’ll still be involved in some sort of fashion at some point. Go down there and do some stuff for them. You know, the Bad News Bears are still going to be a part of my life, and hopefully they continue to win.”
Kisner was informed of the news via a lengthy text message from Woods’ manager Rob McNamara.
“Rob, Tiger’s guy, he text me a long text last week, I think,” Kisner added.
“Just telling me what they did on their decisions, how they were moving around and what players were going to do and that Tiger wanted to play a full schedule.”
Along with Woods and new signing Mitchell, the Jupiter Links roster includes Max Homa, Tom Kim and Akshay Bhatia.
Woods co-founded TGL alongside Rory McIlroy Getty
Season three of TGL begins on December 27.
Which other competitions could Tiger Woods feature in?
Another competition Woods may target to feature in before the year’s end is the Hero World Challenge in December.
Woods hosts the event each year, which brings 20 of the world’s best golfers to the Bahamas.
The field for this year’s tournament has been released and features the likes of Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young and Matt Fitzpatrick.
Curiously, there were three blank spaces on the tee sheet for ‘TBA tournament exemptions’, sparking speculation of Woods’ inclusion.
News of Woods’ mooted comeback follows the 50-year-old hitting balls on the range in September, with his swing looking strong.
He has also kept busy by hosting several golf clinics and making public appearances, including a Q&A session at Pebble Beach.

articles.headline: A Line Held Tight is a charcoal visual novel about a miner's strike in the 32nd century and choosing your relationships wisely
keyFacts: Humble Grove is developing A Line Held Tight, a mecha visual novel about a 32nd-century sci-fi miner's strike.
Players control The Canary and make choices that affect relationships with friends, family, and other workers during the strike.
The game features hand-drawn charcoal art and a traditional folk soundtrack, and currently does not have a release date.
body: We've had about roughly four decades of games as we generally know them now, and yet somehow, so often their stories feel so limited in scope. I'm not talking about a lack of big, bold ideas, in fact there might be too many of those. I more mean that there are aspects to life that often go uncovered in games. For example, when was the last time you saw a game about a workers strike? Citizen Sleeper 2 has one questline about such a thing, but it's just what the entire game is about. A Line Held Tight, a mecha visual novel about a sci-fi miner's strike, may bridge that gap.

A Line Held Tight is being developed by Humble Grove, the studio behind the quiet but impactful No Longer Home. Narrative is at the forefront with this game too, albeit with an emphasis on the choices you make throughout the strike. You play as The Canary, a member of a mining colony who's been cut off by the rest of humanity, set in the 32nd century. "As a strike boils over you’ll help The Canary to decide where their heart and their loyalties lie," the game's Steam page explains. "A branching narrative weaves its way through the deep tunnels of the mine to meet the characters within it as outside influences make themselves felt."

Those aforementioned choices you make primarily affect The Canary's relationships with friends, family and other workers, a much more appealing concept mechanically than simply different endings or storylines. In the world of labour organising, it's the relationships you build with others that's really the key thing, so it's nice to see an emphasis on that both narratively and mechanically. The game has some pretty stunning hand-drawn charcoal art too, as well as a traditional folk soundtrack, a pretty unique combo for a game.

As it stands, A Line Held Tight doesn't currently have a release date. Where it makes up for that is a demo that you can try out right now as part of Steam Next Fest, at the very least. There's a nice little video talking through some of the thought process of making a game such as this one from Humble Grove that you can check out below too. And while you're doing that, whether you check out the demo or not, perhaps give the game a little wishlist on Steam.

articles.headline: AOC says she’s a ‘girl’s girl’ while ripping Dem pols for caving on transgender rights
keyFacts: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez criticized fellow Democrats for compromising on transgender rights during a town hall in Portland, Maine.
Ocasio-Cortez stated that compromising transgender rights threatens the rights of all American citizens.
Ocasio-Cortez also urged Democrats to use congressional committees to investigate the Trump administration.
body: During a town hall in Portland, Maine, a self-described transgender student accused the Democratic Party of abandoning that community, prompting Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) to rip her fellow Dems.
“First and foremost, I want to just let you know how shameful and sorry I am that there are people out there that scare so easily after an election,” she told the student.

“I think it’s what people hate most about politics, which is politicians who will jump on this side or that side of the line at a moment’s notice,” she added. “The moment you compromise the rights of a trans person in America, you compromise the rights of every citizen in America.”

Many Democrats have recalibrated on transgender issues after getting pummeled by Republicans on issues of transgender competitors in women’s sports and the performance of sex change operations on minors.
The possible 2028 presidential contender removed she/her pronouns from her biography on X shortly after President Trump’s victory in 2024.

“There’s plenty of people who may not understand or the conversation about gender may be very new to them, depending on who they are or where they live,” she said. “However, our basic rights shouldn’t have to matter.”
“I don’t support the rights of trans people just to protect my own rights, but I support the rights of trans women because I’m a girl’s girl,” she added with a laugh.
During the wide-ranging question-and-answer session with Jackson, most attendees peppered the “Squad” rep rather than the Maine Senate hopeful.
At one point, she put the Trump administration on blast for the raid on fellow “Squad” Rep. Ilhan Omar’s (D-Minn.) DC home to probe her citizenship status.
Ocasio-Cortez called for Democrats to use congressional committees to turn up the investigative heat on the Trump administration.
“We’ve known the Department of Justice has also been weaponized in its absolutely groundless indictments of everyone from Tish James to Jerome Powell and so on and so forth,” she said.

“Day one, we need to be opening investigations into the head of every single one of these agencies, and we need to hold them accountable. I’m talking subpoenas, I’m talking investigations,” she added. “Everyone must be held to the same standard and rule of law, and we will never get our country back.”
“If we allow criminals to have cabinet seats in the United States of America.”

articles.headline: Would a Democratic Congress change course on Israel?
keyFacts: Voters rarely rank Israel policy among their top priorities, with less than a third prioritizing cutting off aid to Israel according to a poll.
AIPAC announced it would no longer endorse political candidates or make direct campaign contributions.
A Democratic majority in Congress would gain new congressional tools like hearings and funding restrictions, according to analyst Hady Amr.
body: Pro-Palestinian Jewish American demonstrators rally outside AIPAC’s the Manhattan headquarters in February 2024. | Selcuk Acar/Anadolu via Getty Images
This story appeared in Today, Explained, a daily newsletter that helps you understand the most compelling news and stories of the day. Subscribe here .
Israel felt inescapable in the midterm primaries, especially for Democrats, where centrists and progressives clashed — memorably! — over military aid, Gaza, and (of course) AIPAC.

But with the Election Day almost upon us, the subject seems less prominent. When I Googled “Israel US elections” this morning, all the top results concerned next week’s Israeli parliamentary elections.

In less than two weeks, however, Americans will also head to the polls. They’ll decide which party controls Congress, along with a slew of state and local offices. The stakes are arguably unusually high: Voters will choose whether to check the power of a president who has bulldozed over historical norms and limits.

As we count down to that momentous and potentially messy day, I’m partnering with my colleague Astead Herndon and Vox’s The Midterms, Actually team for weekly editions on the biggest issues shaping the midterms. We’re breaking down one issue each week and suggesting further reading and races to watch in November.

Previously, we dug into how both parties are changing , the bipartisan backlash to AI and data centers , and the politics of high costs . This week, we’re tackling Americans’ growing disillusionment with Israel — and how that will (or won’t) show up at the midterm ballot box.
Go a little deeper
View Link
You know the first part of this story already, because we’ve discussed it quite a lot : Americans’ views of Israel have nosedived over the past 18 months.

That shift helped shape the Democratic primaries and will likely figure prominently in the coming presidential contest. But how much Israel matters in a general midterm election, to people outside the political left…well, November will really test that.

Voters rarely rank Israel policy among their top priorities. In a poll that the Associated Press and NORC Center for Public Affairs Research conducted earlier this month, about 80 percent of registered voters said Congress should highly prioritize the cost of living during its next term, and roughly 70 percent said the same about ending the Iran war. By comparison, less than a third of voters said they prioritized cutting off aid to Israel.

There’s another way that Israel factors into US elections, of course — and that’s in fundraising. The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) has become one of the biggest spenders in US elections and a repeat flash point in this year’s Democratic primaries.

But in the general election, even AIPAC has been overshadowed by the GOP’s big-business donors , many of them in tech, who have given Republicans a historic spending advantage in this year’s contests. On Wednesday, the lobbying group actually announced it would no longer endorse political candidates or make direct campaign contributions.

In either case, whatever happens in the midterms won’t likely transform US policy toward Israel. President Donald Trump is still in charge of foreign policy, after all, and even if Democrats take back the House, they’ll have little ability to reverse his agenda.

But a Democratic majority would gain “new congressional tools to act on Israel-Palestine issues,” Hady Amr, the former US Special Representative for Palestinian Affairs, wrote in a new analysis for Chatham House. Those tools aren’t flashy (think: hearings, funding restrictions, and reporting requirements), but they could certainly set the stage for a broader policy shift under a Democratic president.
Races to watch:
Florida’s Senate race , where Democrat Angie Nixon has criticized her party’s ties to the pro-Israel lobby;
Michigan’s Senate race, where Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s campaign grew out of pro-Palestinian activism ;
Michigan’s (deeply purple) Seventh District , where progressive William Lawrence has vocally criticized US support for Israel.
